claim: KTuner staff: Knock Control reflects fuel quality and environment (not just the map).
quote: Knock control is a product of your fuel quality and your environmental factors.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: on the 10th gen 1.5T watch Knock Control, not Knock Count.
quote: Knock Count is not what to watch on this platform.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: an intake with a wrong-sized MAF housing (Injen) gives the ECU wrong airflow, so fueling and knock control suffer; needs a custom tune.
quote: it's not a properly sized MAF housing so the ECU does not get the correct airflow from the MAF sensor.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: do not select the PRL Race MAF basemap option without the PRL Race MAF housing.
quote: Do not use the PRL RACE MAF option if not using a PRL RACE MAF housing.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: Community member (not staff): K.Cont of 0.48 is very good, over 0.80 on a DIY tune is unhappy, over 1.0 find out why (2.0 CVT owner).
quote: .48 is very good. Even on completely factory tune my 2.0 CVT never went below .4X
author: TurboEclipse

claim: KTuner staff: U0301 after flashing a dual-boost map on a 2016 Civic 1.5T means the wrong codebase was chosen in File>New Tune; match it to Tools>KTuner Unit Info.
quote: If you have a U0301 code then you chose the wrong codebase to start from in File>New Tune.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: if the base map feels slower than stock, watch Knock Control; there are quick adjustments for how boost comes in.
quote: Watch knock control to see how the system is performing with your fuel quality and environmental factors.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: boost targets lower than the map (16 vs 19.5 psi, 80% commanded at 100% throttle) mean the tune isn't flashed properly or knock control is pulling back.
quote: or knock control is causing pull back, as we outlined knock control as something to watch.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a 21 psi dual map not exceeding 19.5 psi is due to ECU protections left in place; custom tuning can remove them.
quote: There are several reason why an ECU might limit target boost.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff only referred a 'Starter 21 PSI/Factory Dual' owner reporting 15.x psi top boost at WOT to email support.
quote: Feel free to email support.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: large positive fuel trims in one part of the MAF curve mean that section of the AFM table is wrong/lean.
quote: If it's adding 30% in a particular area of the MAF curve, you've neglected that section and you're running lean.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: STFT is zero in open loop (WOT), so trims only tell you about closed-loop areas.
quote: STFT isn't generally applied at wide open throttle, so it will be zero when in open loop.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a different MAF housing size throws fueling off and needs a custom tune with proper MAF calibration; keep the factory MAF sensor.
quote: If your intake changes the MAF housing size vs factory it will throw fueling off
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a 29 AFR reading when revving is fuel cut (no fuel), not a bad factory tune.
quote: Fuel cut will render 29.4 AFR because there's no fuel.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: exhaust mods need no tune change for gains, but a downpipe may throw an error code; KTuner can't advise disabling emissions equipment.
quote: There's nothing in the tune you need to change to take advantage of exhaust modifications.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: dash/module warnings after flashing a 1.5T CVT Accord clear on their own; KTuner doesn't touch those systems.
quote: You really do just need to wait for those systems to initialize.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: firmware 21 adds 'Clear All Module Errors After Flash' (automatic after firmware update, or a menu option); a user still needed a few miles for the brake system error.
quote: If you update unit firmware it will run it after a flash, too.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: after a flash into limp mode, read codes from the KTuner toolbar and fix what they say.
quote: Check the error codes, which you can do in the KTuner software via the toolbar.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: if LEDs work and the device is in Device Manager, a good cable would at least show a Failure to connect window.
quote: If the LEDs work and the device shows up in device manager
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: V1.2 looping on 'lock to ECU' means the server exchange is timing out (latency); unit blinking blue with key on is unlocked and functional.
quote: If it's looping asking to lock to the ECU that sounds like you're not getting through to the server via the internet.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: 'Exchange incomplete' during registration means the server was reached but timed out; a 'can't contact server' message means something is blocking.
quote: Exchange incomplete means it did connect to the server and either timed out
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a flash persists until reflashed; a car that won't run without the laptop had real-time tuning left enabled.
quote: A flash doesn't get erased until you flash again.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: never flash with the engine running; it can brick the ECU.
quote: The engine should never be running while you flash.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: 'Factory Software Hasn't Been Setup Properly' means tunes were cleared; clear tunes, set up the factory tune with the unit disconnected from the car, then connect to the vehicle.
quote: You cleared tunes or need to load the factory tune again.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: 'Low Voltage on Pin' flash error is the ECU refusing the flash; likely cable or connection (replacement cable via Two Step Performance).
quote: The ECU denied the request to proceed with flashing at that point in the process.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: V1.2 not prompting to lock on a 2017 Civic is usually not fully plugged in or key off; the LED should blink when talking to the ECU.
quote: It sounds like you didn't plug it in fully to the OBD port, didn't key on, or don't have a supported vehicle
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: if 'Disable Closed Loop' can't be checked, use the open-loop transition parameters instead.
quote: You should have parameters for the transition into open loop which you can use to disable it during cruising etc.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: there is a single AFM table; a 'bank 1 too rich' code at idle means fuel trims are far off.
quote: There's only one AFM table.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: 2-step limit-to-restart spread of 200 rpm is Honda's default; a closer spread cuts faster, and Honda's cut is a fuel cut.
quote: 200 is a default Honda uses, so we adopt as well.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: boost cut settings are in PSI; Low/High Cam ignition and fuel maps follow VTEC; IAT corrections follow load.
quote: Boost cut is in PSI Low/High Boost is based on the Low/High switch for boost control.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (2016): boosted-application support for a platform requires custom coding and the ECU part number.
quote: I'd need to custom code the support for it.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (2013): base reflashes are built from a similar dyno-tuned setup; custom tuning gives better results.
quote: You will have better results with custom tuning.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: aftermarket wideband input is only PTANK or ELD on that platform; PTANK/ELD not graphable yet (will look into adding).
quote: ECU inputs likely have a pulldown or pullup.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: there is no way to see which flash is currently running on the ECU.
quote: No.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff declined to explain VTEC/boost/cam tuning; refers users to a professional tuner.
quote: That's what the tuning process is.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: support covers current owners; used-unit buyers must have an unlocked unit.
quote: Our support is always open to current owners of our devices.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Nov 2021, 22+ Civic hatch CVT): included basemaps limit low-end torque for longevity; no parts needed.
quote: The tunes included are safe. We limit low end torque for longevity. Same thing we did for the 10th gen. No parts required.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: lower-boost starter tunes aren't needed for gentle driving; less boost is targeted at less throttle, and which level you use for WOT is the owner's choice.
quote: Yes, less is targeted with less throttle so it's very much based on you.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (May 2022): 11th gen Si gets rev-hang control via Quick Adjustments (throttle), not the overrun throttle compensation field.
quote: If you have the latest build you have the option in quick adjustments for throttle.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a 1.5T that won't start after flashing a TSP tune and won't connect is likely in recovery mode; software offers recovery.
quote: If you failed a flash you're likely in recovery mode and it would give that option.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: VTEC engagement window crossover (mBar) must be found by datalogging; VTEC engaging also affects manifold pressure.
quote: datalogging will be key to finding the right mBar crossover for WOT.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Oct 2023, 2023 Si): there is no dedicated auto start/stop setting on that Si software; available options are in the parameters list.
quote: you will find all currently available options in the parameters list on the left when you open a tune.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: newer-model CAN gateways stop extended CAN data (steering angle, G etc.) from reaching the OBD port.
quote: the CAN Gateway that's been added on all more recent model years will prevent this data from reaching the OBD port.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: with two codebase choices in a basemap, the wrong one gives an error code; check the code and choose the other version.
quote: you likely chose the wrong one to start with because you simply didn't follow the directions in the tune description.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Jan 2020, 2019 Civic 1.5T V1.2): the dual-tune boost target for each on-the-fly tune is chosen via pulldowns; boost by gear is the owner's to set.
quote: We don't setup boost by gear for you. That's something you have control to do.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: ramped Boost By Gear should solve launch traction problems on the 1.5T.
quote: With BBG ramped in you should be able to circumvent traction issues.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Oct 2020, RDX 2.0T): the Turbo Responsiveness quick adjustment only affects targeting and wastegate (EWG) control, not rev hang.
quote: That is for turbo responsiveness only. Targeting and EWG control.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (2018 Accord 1.5T CVT): turbo responsiveness quick adjustment doesn't remove target limits; CVT/stock-clutch cars should limit torque.
quote: The target limits for the turbo are still enforced with this setting.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: with a factory clutch or CVT, keep torque limited even with a downpipe.
quote: if you have a factory clutch or a CVT model you do want to limit torque output
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (2018): early spool doesn't cause overboost; torque is limited by the tune itself, not torque management, and boost targets are not high.
quote: Early spool is safe and does not cause overboost.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (2018 Accord 1.5T CVT): starter tunes cover exhaust mods; an intake that changes MAF housing size can throw fueling off.
quote: The tune covers exhaust mods. Improperly designed intakes that alter the MAF housing size may throw fueling off.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: no deeper explanation of Early Spool vs Turbo Responsiveness than the help page; owner should try settings against factory.
quote: early spool and turbo responsiveness affect spool and responsiveness of the turbo.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: fix the MAF curve for a new intake before touching AFR targets; more air means more fuel used.
quote: You shouldn't be messing with AFR targets until you've fixed the MAF curve for that intake.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Feb 2023, Accord 1.5T): MAF only needs rescaling for housing or flow changes; WOT Enrichment targets control wide-open AFR.
quote: MAF should only need to be scaled for a MAF housing change or change in flow dynamics with aftermarket intake piping.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: WOT enrichment targets only work if the base fuel tables give 14.7; change fuel tables, not just WOT targets.
quote: It assumes the fuel tables are tuned for a perfect 14.7 in order for the enrichments to reach targets.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: a separate WOT enrichment table applies in catalyst-heating mode; AFR.CMD in the data list shows which table is active.
quote: CAT HEATING mode is when the ECU decides it's necessary to heat the catalyst.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Feb 2021, Element turbo): K.Count and K.Control are separate ECU systems; K.Cont rose 0.8 to 1.2 with almost no knock count.
quote: You're correct in assuming that K.Count and K.Control are different systems within the ECU.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: knock count at startup is normal; watch Knock Control for real movement.
quote: Knock count isn't what to watch on this platform, but most platforms may see startup counts.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: KTuner doesn't touch the transmission controller; CVT/trans problems may show up sooner with tune demand.
quote: We don't flash the transmission controller, so if you're stalling the transmission could be the entire cause
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: for odd Knock Control after an octane booster, try a different gas station and skip the booster.
quote: The octane booster may not be helping either. I'd probably not use it.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: boost is relative pressure, so at elevation the turbo still makes the same relative psi (absolute is lower).
quote: Sea Level - 15-0=15 Absolute/15 Relative to Atmospheric (0)
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: TunerView Lite on a rooted 2020 Civic: key fully on (two clicks), unit flashing green, BT PIN settings per online help for 18-20 models.
quote: Set the BT settings to what's mentioned in the Online Help for 18-20 model Civics.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: most aftermarket Android head units can't connect to the KTuner unit over Bluetooth; one worked only with fiddly third-party apps.
quote: most of the aftermarket head units aren't capable of connecting to a device like ours directly
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: after flashing the wrong ECU-matched codebase on a 2016 Civic 1.5T, start a new tune with the other codebase.
quote: If you chose the wrong option because you didn't do that, start a new tune and choose the other one.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: errors can be cleared with the KTuner unit; there are no checkboxes for P0139/P0159/P0400.
quote: You can clear errors with the unit, so disconnecting the battery is unnecessary.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: V1.2/V2 can store multiple tunes (e.g. stock and stage 2) and flash from the display or TunerView app; flashing isn't on-the-fly.
quote: The unit can store multiple tunes to flash either on the display or with the TunerView app
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: on turbo Honda DBW the Final table takes the standard table's output; Final and ECO should not match each other.
quote: The Final DBW table uses the output of the standard table as it's incoming TP value.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff: no anti-lag planned for the FK8.
quote: Information suggests engines have been blown from using this feature on other platforms.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)

claim: KTuner staff (Dec 2024, Civic Platform): DTC U129E is a communications error and wouldn't change fueling; a fuel smell is not a tuning cause if the tune has run correctly since 2020.
quote: U129E is a communication error that wouldn't affect fueling.
author: KTuner (Site Admin)
